To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we develop a deep neural network that is capable of simultaneously denoising and decomposing seismic data and we show that this approach is capable of significantly increasing signal-to-noise-ratio and improving the detection of earthquakes.

we develop a new method for denoising/decomposing seismic signals, DeepDenoising, that is able to learn a sparse representation of the input signals and a non-linear mapping that decomposes the signals into signal of interest and any non-earthquake noise, and that DeepDenoising achieves impressive denoises even when the signal of interest and the noise share a common spectral band.

we developed a new method, DeepDENOISER, based on deep neural networks that is able to learn the sparse representation of data and the non-linear mapping of this representation into masks, that decompose input signals into signal and noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a new method that is capable of denoising seismic signals and decomposing the data into signal of interest and non-seismic noise.
the development of a new denoiser that can be used for seismic-data-processing and for a variety of other applications.
the application of deep learning to seismic signal analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DeepDenoisers is a novel and effective approach for denoising and decomposing seismic data.

our method can be applied to any signal that can be represented as a linear sum of a signal of interest (that can be represented as sparse in a certain domain) and noise, which is the most general form of signal decomposition.
we developed a new method, DeepDENOISER, for the seismic denoising problem, which is based on a deep learning approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a new deep-learning method to improve the SNR and to decompose signals of interest from noisy signals.
we develop a novel deep neural network for denoising and decomposition of seismic signals.

we developed a new denoiser that can learn a sparse representation of seismic data in the timefrequency domain and a non-linearity that maps this representation to a decomposition of input data into a seismic signal and nonseismic noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DeepDenoisers are powerful tools for seismic signal processing and can be adapted to many applications.
deep learning is a powerful tool for signal processing in seismology, and that it can be applied to many different types of problems.
deep neural networks can be used to learn a non-linear function, in this case a mask that decomposes input data into a seismic signal and a nonseismic noise.
